In 206 BC, [Scipio Africanus](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%8A%A4%ED%82%A4%ED%94%BC%EC%98%A4%20%EC%95%84%ED%94%84%EB%A6%AC%EC%B9%B4%EB%88%84%EC%8A%A4 "Scipio Africanus") pacified the Iberian Peninsula after winning a decisive victory over the Carthaginian army under [Hasdrubal Gisco](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%95%98%EC%8A%A4%EB%93%9C%EB%A3%A8%EB%B0%9C%20%EA%B8%B0%EC%8A%A4%EC%BD%94 "Hasdrubal Gisko") - [Mago Barca](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%A7%88%EA%B3%A0%20%EB%B0%94%EB%A5%B4%EC%B9%B4 "Margot Barca") at [the Battle of Ilipa](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%9D%BC%EB%A6%AC%ED%8C%8C%20%EC%A0%84%ED%88%AC "Battle of Ilipa") . After returning to Rome, he was elected [consul](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%A7%91%EC%A0%95%EA%B4%80 "consul") in 205 BC and announced his intention to end the war by attacking North Africa and subduing Carthage. Elders such as [Quintus Fabius Maximus,](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%80%B8%ED%88%AC%EC%8A%A4%20%ED%8C%8C%EB%B9%84%EC%9A%B0%EC%8A%A4%20%EB%A7%89%EC%8B%9C%EB%AC%B4%EC%8A%A4 "Quintus Fabius Maximus") the Roman army under [Marcus Atilius Regulus, who](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%A7%88%EB%A5%B4%EC%BF%A0%EC%8A%A4%20%EC%95%84%ED%8B%B8%EB%A6%AC%EC%9A%B0%EC%8A%A4%20%EB%A0%88%EA%B5%B4%EB%A3%A8%EC%8A%A4 "Marcus Atilius Regulus") had undertaken an expedition to Africa in 255 BC, was defeated and captured by the Carthaginian army led by [Xanthippus](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%81%AC%EC%82%B0%ED%8B%B0%ED%91%B8%EC%8A%A4 "xanthoid fever") at [the Battle of Baggradas](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%B0%94%EA%B7%B8%EB%9D%BC%EB%8B%A4%EC%8A%A4%20%EC%A0%84%ED%88%AC "Battle of Bagradas") , and the Roman fleet led the defeated soldiers to escape to their homeland. Reminding the incident that suffered severe human casualties in a marine accident while doing so, he insisted, "Now we must focus on defeating Hannibal, and not strike Africa."

However, Scipio did not back down and demanded that he take full responsibility for the expedition to Africa, saying that it was impossible to defeat Hannibal while he was holding out in Brutium. The public sentiment also wanted to end the long-lasting war as soon as possible, so when Scipio's argument was enthusiastically supported, the Senate dispatched Scipio to Sicily to prepare for an expedition. However, since no regular army was entrusted to him, Scipio was sent to Sicily as punishment after defeat at [the Battle of Cannae](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%B9%B8%EB%82%98%EC%9D%B4%20%EC%A0%84%ED%88%AC "battle of kannai") and other battles, where he recruited the Roman remnants and trained them for a year. At the same time, he entrusted his close friend and lieutenant, [Gaius Lailius,](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B0%80%EC%9D%B4%EC%9A%B0%EC%8A%A4%20%EB%9D%BC%EC%9D%BC%EB%A6%AC%EC%9A%B0%EC%8A%A4 "Gaius Rylius") with a navy to plunder the coast of Africa. In response, Carthage sent envoys to [the Kingdom of Macedon](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%A7%88%EC%BC%80%EB%8F%84%EB%8B%88%EC%95%84%20%EC%99%95%EA%B5%AD "kingdom of macedonia") to ask [Philip V](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%95%84%EB%A6%AC%ED%8F%AC%EC%8A%A4%205%EC%84%B8 "Philip the 5th") to invade Sicily, but Philip V refused, saying he had already signed a peace treaty with Rome. Here, [Mago Barca](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%A7%88%EA%B3%A0%20%EB%B0%94%EB%A5%B4%EC%B9%B4 "Margot Barca") landed in Genoa and joined Hannibal, but he was also stopped at [the Battle of Insubria](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%9D%B8%EC%88%98%EB%B8%8C%EB%A6%AC%EC%95%84%20%EC%A0%84%ED%88%AC "Battle of Insubria") and settled in Genoa.

Scipio tried to attack Carthage by allying with [Siphax](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%8B%9C%ED%8C%8D%EC%8A%A4 "Sifax") , king of the Massaecili tribe, traditionally hostile to Carthage. However, when the Carthaginian senate forced Sophonisba, who had been betrothed to Masinissa, a prince of the Massili tribe, to [marry Siphax](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%A7%88%EC%8B%9C%EB%8B%88%EC%82%AC "Masinissa") , Siphax decided to join hands with Carthage. Afterwards, Siphax and his father-in-law, [Hasdrubal Ghisco,](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%95%98%EC%8A%A4%EB%93%9C%EB%A3%A8%EB%B0%9C%20%EA%B8%B0%EC%8A%A4%EC%BD%94 "Hasdrubal Gisko") attacked the Masili tribe in a pincer attack and quickly subdued them and took over all of Numidia. Masinissa hid in the desert with only a few of his men. Scipio was disappointed to hear of this, but he did not give up on the invasion plan.

In 204 BC, Scipio landed on Cape Farina, about 20 miles (35 km) west of Carthage, carrying some 35,000 men on hundreds of transport ships. He sent out raiding parties to various nearby villages to plunder to their heart's content. [Hasdrubal Gisco](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%95%98%EC%8A%A4%EB%93%9C%EB%A3%A8%EB%B0%9C%20%EA%B8%B0%EC%8A%A4%EC%BD%94 "Hasdrubal Gisko") sent a cavalry force to prevent further plunder and stop the movement of the enemy, but the Romans defeated them near the town of Salaeca. With the addition of Masinissa, the Roman cavalry was further strengthened. Having thus secured considerable booty and slaves, Scipio marched on Utica. He intended to capture Utica and make it his outpost. However, he mobilized all siege weapons and sent in the navy, but when the attack failed, he besieged Utica and tried to kill its citizens.

A few days later, word came that a large army of Hasdurbal Gisko and Siphax was advancing. According to [Titus Livius Patavinus](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%8B%B0%ED%88%AC%EC%8A%A4%20%EB%A6%AC%EB%B9%84%EC%9A%B0%EC%8A%A4%20%ED%8C%8C%ED%83%80%EB%B9%84%EB%88%84%EC%8A%A4 "Titus Livius Patavius") and [Polybius](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%8F%B4%EB%A6%AC%EB%B9%84%EC%98%A4%EC%8A%A4 "polybius") , Hasdrubal's army numbered more than 30,000 men, while Siphax's had twice that. Modern scholars consider this figure to be exaggerated, but it is highly likely that Carthage and Numidia fought an all-out war, hoping to somehow drive the Romans from the mainland. Scipio decided to retreat for the first time to Cape Castra Cornelia, not far from Utica, fortify it, and camp for the winter with provisions and winter clothes from Sicily, Sardinia, and Iberia. Hasdrubal and Siphax set up camp not far from there and confronted the Romans.

Scipio, observing the situation, knew that Hasdrubal Gisco was mobilizing a fleet to block the sea and cut off the Roman army's supply lines, so he decided to strike first. However, there were so many enemies that I couldn't attack hastily and watched the situation. In the meantime, when Siphax offered to mediate the negotiations, he responded by sending an envoy to the Carthaginian army. Hasdrubal Gisco proposed that Rome and Carthage withdraw their invasion forces from Italy and Africa. Scipio had no intention of accepting this, but the negotiations continued.

He initially tried to coax Masinissa's old men, who belonged to Siphax, to no avail. Accordingly, he continued to send his envoys to find out what the defenses of the enemy camp were like under the pretense of negotiating. After some time, envoys reported the location and defense system of the enemy camp, notably that the two encampments of the Carthaginian and Numidian forces consisted of huts built of wood, reeds, and fire-resistant materials. In response, Scipio decided to make a fire attack by raiding at night, and ordered the entire army to prepare for battle.

According to [Polybius](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%8F%B4%EB%A6%AC%EB%B9%84%EC%98%A4%EC%8A%A4 "polybius") and [Titus Livius Patavius](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%8B%B0%ED%88%AC%EC%8A%A4%20%EB%A6%AC%EB%B9%84%EC%9A%B0%EC%8A%A4%20%ED%8C%8C%ED%83%80%EB%B9%84%EB%88%84%EC%8A%A4 "Titus Livius Patavius") , Scipio moved a force of 2,000 men into the hills near Utica to deceive enemy scouts by giving the impression that he was preparing to attack the city. Another small detachment was left behind to protect the Roman camp from attacks by the garrison of Utica, while the rest of the army marched more than 10 km during the night and reached the camp of Hasdrubal and Syphax before dawn. Scipio divided his army into two , under the command of [Gaius Lalius](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B0%80%EC%9D%B4%EC%9A%B0%EC%8A%A4%20%EB%9D%BC%EC%9D%BC%EB%A6%AC%EC%9A%B0%EC%8A%A4 "Gaius Rylius") and [Masinissa](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%A7%88%EC%8B%9C%EB%8B%88%EC%82%AC "Masinissa") , and set fire to Syphax's camp and destroyed it. The entire Numidian camp was burned by this fire, and many Numidian soldiers were slaughtered by the enemy or trampled to death while trying to escape. When the Carthaginians saw the neighboring camp burning, they thought it was an accident and tried to extinguish the fire, but were attacked by Scipio's army and suffered numerous casualties. It is said that only a small unit protecting Hasdrubal and Syphax succeeded in escaping.

According to [Appianus](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%95%84%ED%94%BC%EC%95%84%EB%85%B8%EC%8A%A4 "Appianos") , in order to prevent Syphax from aiding Hasdrubal, Scipio detached Masinissa and his cavalry to keep Syphax in check. Afterwards, he led his entire army and attacked Hasdrubal's camp, setting fire to the enemy camp and slaughtering the confused enemies. Syphax saw fire rising from a neighboring camp and decided that something was amiss, so he dispatched cavalry, but was defeated by Masinisa. Afterwards, he was afraid that Scipio would come to deal with him as well, so he abandoned the camp and retreated to a safe place.

According to ancient texts, between 30,000 and 40,000 Carthaginians were killed and 5,000 captured. Most sources describe Roman losses as minimal, but [Cassius Dio](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%94%94%EC%98%A4%20%EC%B9%B4%EC%8B%9C%EC%9A%B0%EC%8A%A4 "Dio Cassius") writes that a belatedly arriving Iberian mercenary force attacked the next morning, killing many unsuspecting Romans and returning. After winning Utica's submission, Scipio won Utica's submission and marched to Carthage, where he faced the Carthaginian-Numidian allied forces again at Bagradas ( [Battle of Bagradas](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%B0%94%EA%B7%B8%EB%9D%BC%EB%8B%A4%EC%8A%A4%20%EC%A0%84%ED%88%AC(%EA%B8%B0%EC%9B%90%EC%A0%84%20203%EB%85%84) "Battle of Bagradas (203 BC)") ) .
